description: Machine-readable index of completed local backup/restore foundations. These drills are exact-source executable evidence, including a shared PostgreSQL/object recovery-set binding, but are not PostgreSQL PITR, independent provider retention, temporal recovery-point skew measurement, approved RPO/RTO or production disaster-recovery evidence.

proves: canonical migration sequence applies to an ephemeral source database
custom-format pg_dump restores into a separate empty database
all canonical SQL integration tests pass on the restored database in migration order
four runtime roles retain NOBYPASSRLS
tenant tables retain FORCE RLS
synthetic deleted account and session digest do not resurrect
deleted synthetic token cannot resolve through memory_auth_runtime
synthetic expired active session row remains expired after restore and cannot resolve through memory_auth_runtime
synthetic revoked unexpired session row remains revoked after restore and cannot resolve through memory_auth_runtime
doesNotProve: production backup schedule or independent retention

proves: three source object versions are created in a versioned local MinIO bucket
a non-latest source version is selected explicitly
the selected version is copied to a separate backup bucket with source-version binding metadata
all source versions and delete markers are removed before recovery
the exact backup version restores to a third bucket
checksum, length and source-version binding survive recovery
provider version identifiers are distinct and stored only as digests in evidence
doesNotProve: coherent PostgreSQL and object recovery point

proves: one opaque synthetic recovery-set digest is persisted in PostgreSQL state and exact-version object metadata before backup
source PostgreSQL database and source object versions are destroyed before recovery verification
database logical backup and exact object backup restore into separate targets
restored PostgreSQL state independently yields the expected recovery-set digest
restored object metadata independently yields the expected recovery-set digest
restored database and object recovery-set digests are identical
exact backup object checksum survives restore
a deliberately one-sided recovery-set digest mismatch is rejected fail-closed
doesNotProve: production TLS or restore-only credential separation
